title: Build batch table
description: One dependency-closed batch of backlog phases, in the order a coordinator builds them. Phase facts (scope, acceptance, systems, deliverables, depends_on) live in docs/09-backlog/backlog.yaml and are never restated here; a batch table records only how a set of phases is grouped, sequenced and parallelised for one coordinator run.

id.description: Table identity, matching its filename stem prefix. Not a governed document code — batch tables are data, like backlog.yaml, and are not allocated through --next-code.

title.description: What this batch builds, in a phrase a person can read without opening the backlog.

status.description: Run state of the table itself, not of its phases. 'queued' is runnable and unstarted; 'in_progress' means a coordinator run is open against it and must be resumed rather than restarted; 'complete' means every phase reached complete; 'superseded' means the composition was replaced and the table is kept for history only. A superseded table is never selected to run.

superseded_by.description: Required in spirit whenever status is 'superseded': the table that replaced this one.

sequence.description: Position in the intended run order across all tables. The coordinator selects the lowest-sequence runnable table; a tie is what makes selection ambiguous and forces it to ask the owner.

updated.description: Date of the last substantive edit to the table.

coordinator.description: The prompt pack that runs this table, by code — normally PROMPT-036.

provenance.description: Where the composition came from and how it was checked. A partition asserted without a recorded check is the failure this field exists to prevent.

verified.description: The last time the composition was checked against the backlog. A coordinator re-verifies before running regardless of how recent this is; the field records history, it does not license skipping the check.

external_depends_on.description: Phases outside this batch that every one of its dependency edges resolves to. Each must be complete before the batch runs; a batch is dependency-closed only against these.

excluded.description: Phases deliberately kept out of this batch though they sit in next_up, each with the reason. An exclusion recorded nowhere is indistinguishable from an omission.

stages.description: Ordered build stages. A stage begins only after every phase in the preceding stage is complete and integrated. Phases within one stage carry no dependency edge and no systems or deliverables collision between them, so they may be claimed and built concurrently.

stage.description: 1-based position; must equal the entry's index in the list.

parallel.description: Whether this stage's phases may run concurrently. True requires more than one phase. It is a permission, not an instruction: the coordinator still checks max_active and the Conflicts column numerically before every claim, and a stage of three runs serially when the budget has room for one.

rationale.description: Why this stage is cut where it is — normally the collision or dependency that stops its phases joining the stage before.

phases.description: Phases in this stage. When parallel is false, they are built in listed order.

id.description: Phase id, which must exist in backlog.yaml.

title.description: The phase's backlog title, copied so a reader need not open the backlog. Convenience only; the backlog is authoritative.

after.description: Phases in this same batch that this phase depends on, drawn from its backlog depends_on. Empty when it has no in-batch dependency. Every entry must sit in an earlier stage.

conflicts_with.description: Phases in this batch that share a system or an overlapping deliverable path with this one, and so can never occupy its stage. This is why a phase with no dependency can still be forced to run late — the reason is a lock, not an ordering.

notes.description: Anything a coordinator should know before running this table that no other field carries.
